source_review.notes: Reviewed the primary Bernstein-Goodman MVCC paper; Bernstein-Hadzilacos-Goodman text; current PostgreSQL 18 MVCC, isolation, vacuum, freeze, and wraparound documentation; MySQL 8.4 multiversion, consistent-read, secondary-index, undo, and purge documentation; current SQL Server 17 row-versioning/version-store guidance; and the primary Cahill-Rohm-Fekete SSI paper. All ten cited destinations were retrieved and retained locally. Current storage, snapshot, cleanup, and failure claims are product/version/configuration scoped.

evidence: Checked logical item/version history, creator, transaction status, commit order, snapshot, visibility, latest-visible, tombstone, conflict, observer obligations, reclamation horizon, version debt, and write-skew notation.
Checked physical version, logical row, transaction ID, commit sequence, active set, wall clock, version chain, and index membership are not used interchangeably.
Checked scalar teaching snapshot is explicitly distinguished from PostgreSQL, InnoDB, and SQL Server metadata/rules.
Checked all point-read claims include at-most-one logical result and deletion/own-write handling.
notation_and_syntax.notes: MVCC mechanism, isolation policy, writer coordination, recovery, indexing, and cleanup are modeled as separate composable responsibilities.

evidence: Independently represented committed versions as half-open intervals [1,4), [4,7), and [7,infinity), rather than using the chapter's maximum-commit implementation.
Recomputed snapshots 3,5,8 as values 100,120,135 and snapshot 10 as committed value 135 while T4's active value remains invisible to another owner.
Recomputed own-write value 150, active-snapshot horizon min(5,8)=5, and predecessor v1 as the only interval ending at or before the horizon.
Recomputed retained versions v2,v3,v4 and independent_invariants=True.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The independent interval calculation is retained at artifacts/reviews/DBE-046/independent-recomputation.txt.

evidence: Re-derived unique newest committed version selection under strictly ordered unique commit sequences.
Re-derived horizon safety: successor commit <= minimum active snapshot makes the predecessor unreachable by every active/future scalar snapshot.
Re-derived the retain boundary when successor commit exceeds the horizon.
Constructed active-set, replica, backup, time-travel, rollback, and distributed-order countercases showing why a scalar local horizon can be incomplete.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The reclamation theorem assumes total atomic commit order, monotone snapshots, complete obligations, and no omitted transaction-local/recovery requirement.

evidence: Reviewed empty history, first insert, just-before/at/after commit, active/aborted/own candidates, delete, reinsert, key change, multiple physical matches, and commit-publication crash boundaries.
Reviewed concurrent same-row writers, lost update, disjoint write skew, phantoms, unique/foreign-key checks, locking/current reads, writer deadlock, and serializable validation.
Reviewed append, undo-reconstruction, external store, full/delta versions, secondary indexes, covering scans, dead memberships, and cleanup/index races.

Reviewed long/idle readers, replicas, backups, online operations, CDC/time travel, chain depth, bloat, undo/version-store exhaustion, cleanup lag, write throttling, wraparound/freeze, cancellation, and rollback cost.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cleanup recommendations require complete reachability evidence and protect data/recovery invariants before reclaiming space.

evidence: The repository verifier matched exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status for the visibility/reclamation model.
The model checks snapshot results, read-your-writes, exclusion of another owner's active candidate, horizon, exact reclaimable and retained sets.

Manual review checked stable logical identity, durable outcome/order metadata, at-most-one result, abort exclusion, write-head coordination, index equivalence, complete observer obligations, and identifier-order safety.
Draft validation accepted exact front matter, section order, ten examples, five exercises/answers, links, citations, and executable evidence before stopping only for review evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: The model omits active-set snapshots, deletes, indexes, locking, concurrent publication, crash recovery, replicas, vendor metadata, and physical cleanup.

evidence: Reviewed selection proof from admitted committed set through unique maximum and own-write override.
Reviewed reclamation proof from complete observer set and minimum snapshot through successor reachability, plus failure assumptions.
Reviewed write-safety argument showing that visibility cannot replace logical-head coordination or predicate-level serializability.
Reviewed all exercise answers for boundary visibility, proof/counterexamples, implementation/crash oracles, layout capacity, and cross-engine incident response.
proof_review.notes: No proof of vendor MVCC correctness, serializability of snapshot isolation, distributed timestamp order, cleanup completeness, crash recovery, or production capacity is claimed.

evidence: The selection and reclamation arguments are explicitly labeled simplified proofs with their scalar-model assumptions.
The executable code is explicitly a teaching abstraction rather than vendor visibility pseudocode.
PostgreSQL/InnoDB/SQL Server examples distinguish official current layouts from the durable abstract model.
Audited visible, committed, snapshot, current, safe, reclaimable, unique, prevents, serializable, never blocks, complete, and durable language for scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter repeatedly states that MVCC does not itself define isolation or guarantee serializability.

evidence: The standard-library visibility/horizon model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
A separate interval representation independently reproduced all reads and retained/reclaimable versions.
All ten primary/official sources were retrieved and inspected for the cited claims.
Production conclusions require engine/version/configuration, snapshot/pin owners, version generation, cleanup, chain depth, storage, plan/index, conflicts, recovery, latency, and invariant evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live MVCC engine, concurrent writer, vacuum/purge, version store, index cleanup, crash, replica, backup, wraparound harness, space exhaustion, or workload benchmark was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter develops MVCC from logical version identity through snapshots, visibility, writer publication, physical organizations, index semantics, safe reclamation, and the boundary with isolation/serializability.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current PostgreSQL tuple/vacuum/freeze, InnoDB undo/purge/index, and SQL Server version-store/RCSI/SNAPSHOT behavior plus long-snapshot capacity, observability, incident response, and recovery testing.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, executable version trace, scoped proofs, ten distinct examples, and five exercises progress from version selection through implementation, layout tradeoffs, and unfamiliar production diagnosis.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter does not certify a vendor visibility implementation, isolation configuration, writer policy, recovery path, index/version layout, cleanup horizon, capacity model, replica/backup integration, or production deployment.
